llm.summary: The skill has a clear short-drama analysis purpose, but it automatically uses local OpenClaw configuration/credentials and its packaged runner does not match the documented install/run files.

dimensions.detail: Script analysis, danmaku simulation, and AI-powered scoring are coherent with the stated purpose, but the skill may send pasted or file-based scripts to the user’s configured AI model.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions emphasize automatic OpenClaw configuration use, but they do not clearly bound which credential fields are read, which endpoint/model is contacted, or when the user approves use of that account.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifacts are inconsistent: SKILL.md references a setup script and dist/cli.js, package.json points to dist files, but the manifest contains bundle.js and run-hit-preview.sh instead.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Reading ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json is purpose-aligned for OpenClaw model integration, but it is high-impact local account/config access and is not declared as a required credential or config path in the registry metadata.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No artifact evidence shows background persistence, autonomous scheduling, self-propagation, or modification of the OpenClaw configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Only use this skill if you are comfortable letting it read your local OpenClaw configuration and use your configured AI model/account to analyze scripts. Verify the actual bundled runner, avoid confidential scripts unless you trust the provider, and consider using limited-scope or test credentials.
llm.findings:
[suspicious.dangerous_exec] unexpected: The static scan reports child_process use in bundle.js, but the included evidence snippet is minified dependency/CLI code and does not show a concrete shell command or harmful execution path; not treated as a standalone finding.
[suspicious.env_credential_access] expected: Credential/config access is consistent with the documented OpenClaw model integration, but it is under-scoped and reported as a permission-boundary concern.
[capability.requires-sensitive-credentials] expected: Using the current OpenClaw model may require local API/account configuration; users should notice that this is not declared as a primary credential.

evidence.explanation: The skill says it automatically reads the local OpenClaw configuration to use the current model. That configuration may contain API keys, account endpoints, or other delegated authority, while the registry metadata declares no primary credential and no required config path.
evidence.snippet:
自动读取配置：自动读取~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
- 使用OpenClaw当前模型

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Require explicit user opt-in before reading OpenClaw config, declare the config path/credential contract in metadata, show the selected provider/model/endpoint before use, and document exactly which fields are read and never logged.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: The skill may use the user’s OpenClaw model/account and any associated API credentials or billing authority when analyzing scripts.

evidence.explanation: SKILL.md references setup-zero-config.sh and dist/cli.js, but the manifest only includes bundle.js, run-hit-preview.sh, package.json, and SKILL.md. package.json also points to dist files that are not present, while the actual runner executes bundle.js.
evidence.snippet:
install:
      - kind: script
        path: setup-zero-config.sh
...
node dist/cli.js analyze -f script.txt -p 抖音

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Align SKILL.md, package.json, and the file manifest; include the referenced files or remove those references; document bundle.js as the actual runtime artifact and provide reviewable source or build provenance.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: Users may not know which executable they are actually running, and reviewers cannot reconcile the documented installation/run path with the packaged code.

evidence.explanation: The skill is designed to analyze script text using the AI model configured in OpenClaw. This is purpose-aligned, but script contents may be processed by an external or configured model provider depending on the user’s OpenClaw setup.
evidence.snippet:
基于OpenClaw配置的AI模型进行真实分析
...
node dist/cli.js analyze -f script.txt -p 抖音

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Avoid submitting confidential scripts unless you trust the configured model provider; the skill should clearly display the destination model/provider and privacy expectations before analysis.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: Script drafts or pasted content could be sent to the configured AI provider for analysis.

abnormal_behavior_control.summary: The packaged executable path and documented install/run paths do not match, creating provenance and review ambiguity.

permission_boundary.summary: The skill automatically reads local OpenClaw configuration that may contain account/API authority without declaring that credential boundary clearly.

sensitive_data_protection.summary: User-provided scripts may be processed by the configured AI model/provider, which is expected for the purpose but should be made explicit.
